# aibris v0.14.0

This release hardens every deletion against stale or incomplete evidence,
makes cancellation reliable, gives `size` one documented meaning, and gates
publication on verification of the exact release commit. It remediates the
2026-10-07 engineering audit (#581-#584).

## Highlights

- **Re-verified at the moment of deletion.**
  - A worktree that a cached scan called orphaned is checked against current
    Git evidence right before removal, including changes made while you
    confirm. A restored parent repository, a replaced marker, or a new member
    refuses the deletion (#585).
  - Claude session metadata now reads an escaped spelling of the `cwd` key
    (such as `\u0063wd`) as `cwd`, so a live owner recorded that way is
    found. A record with a duplicate `cwd` key, escaped or not, is no longer
    ownership evidence; unless another record proves a live owner, the store
    stays `undetermined` (#586).
  - Incomplete activity evidence (unreadable subtree, I/O error, mid-walk
    cancellation) no longer approves age-based deletion (#589).
- **Cleanup commands come from the live catalog** (#587). Cached command lines
  are inventory only. A changed, unknown, or tampered recipe is refused with
  `cleanup_recipe_changed`. Homebrew's cache is now removed through the gated
  path route instead of `brew cleanup --prune=all`, so installed kegs are never
  touched.
- **Cancellation everywhere** (#594). The final, per-item, guided, unified, and
  APFS confirmations all return promptly on Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. Targets that had
  not started are kept and reported as cancelled.
- **One `size` meaning** (#598). `size` is apparent bytes from one walker on
  every platform. Sparse files count their logical length. On Unix a
  hardlinked file counts once per target. Symlinks below a target are not
  followed. The `du` fast path is gone, so a missing or odd `du` no longer
  changes the numbers.
- **Faster, single-plan execution** (#590, #591). Review, JSON, and execution
  share one plan per run with typed prepared evidence. Plan construction no
  longer scales cubically. On one machine, `BenchmarkUnifiedCleanupPlan` with
  2,000 independent targets went from about 24 s to about 3 s.
- **Codex activity across every configured home** (#592). Activity follows the
  same homes as discovery. An unreadable home is no longer treated as "no
  recent activity".
- **Stable JSON reasons** (#596). `activity_source_not_registered`,
  `cleanup_recipe_changed`, and `worktree_evidence_changed` reach the final
  plan and receipt.
- **Release and install trust** (#593, #595, #588).
  - Publishing and the Homebrew tap update now require the full verification
    suite to pass on the tagged commit itself.
  - Privileged actions and release tools are pinned.
  - The installers keep the existing binary on every failure path; tests
    exercise the real scripts.
- **Docs** (#599, #600). Current contracts are separated from dated history.
  The unregistered Codex tmp implementation stays documented as unsupported.

## Compatibility impact

- [x] **Compatible addition.** New receipt reason codes
  `cleanup_recipe_changed` and `worktree_evidence_changed`. No flag, field, or
  enum value was removed or renamed, and `schema_version` stays `1`.
- [x] **Byte accounting specified.** v0.13.0 documented `size` only as a
  size in bytes. In practice it was `du` allocated blocks when `du` worked and
  apparent bytes otherwise. The field's type and documented meaning (bytes)
  are unchanged, so `schema_version` stays `1`. Its byte accounting is now
  specified in `docs/JSON_SCHEMA.md`, and sizes differ from v0.13.0 output.
  - Trees of many small files, such as `node_modules`, usually look somewhat
    smaller, because block rounding is no longer counted.
  - Sparse files can look larger.

## Upgrade and migration

No flag migration is required.

```bash
brew upgrade aibris
# or (Unix):
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.sh | bash -s -- v0.14.0
# or (Windows PowerShell):
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

- The first run rebuilds the last-scan cache, because size meaning changed
  under a new cache revision.
- Automation that compared sizes across versions should re-baseline.
- aibris no longer prunes old Homebrew kegs. Run `brew cleanup` yourself if
  you want that.

## Safety

- Every earlier safeguard is unchanged: the single deletion gate, dry-run and
  confirmation, `--risky`, active-worktree protection, agent-state proof and
  grace, snapshot identity, overlap safety, and strip re-authorization. This
  release adds checks at the mutation boundary; it removes none.
- An orphaned worktree whose `.git` marker is a symlink is always refused
  (fail-closed).
- Known limitations, tracked for follow-up:
  - npm cleanup can still write `<cache>/_logs`, and `go clean -cache` can
    trigger a toolchain download from a module directory (#605).
  - Some cleaner command tests do not run on Windows (#602).

## Windows status

Changed from v0.13.0: native Windows CI now runs the full
`internal/safedelete`, `internal/pathidentity`, and `internal/testutil`
packages. The existing PowerShell installer tests now exercise the production
`install.ps1` failure paths instead of inline copies of its guards (#595). Real vendor agent
worktree layouts on Windows, end-to-end delete mutation, and native arm64
execution remain experimental and unmeasured. See `docs/WINDOWS.md`.
